scientificAndNumericalReview: The measurements disagree with the specified point-launch prediction. They do not establish how much of the disagreement was caused by tipping. That distinction affects a compulsory scoring criterion. For parts 1–3, the mean phase accelerations are +1.333…, 0 and −2.0 m/s². The successive two-second means in phase I are 1.6, 1.6 and 0.8 m/s², so acceleration decreases in the last interval. The five trapezoidal areas are 3.2, 9.6, 14.4, 16.0 and 12.0 m, totalling 55.2 m. Since all velocities are nonnegative, that area also gives distance travelled. The nominal point model gives t₀ = √(2 × 1.25/9.81) = 0.50481878 s and x₀ = 8t₀ = 4.0385502 m. The reported 0.505 s and 4.04 m are correctly rounded.
partOneToThreePreservationReview: The exact file matches the sealed proposal object and its raw SHA-256. Independent comparison reproduces all 13 delta paths and their before/after values. Materials 1–3, the calculation note, numbered prompts 1–4, worked solutions 1–4 and complete s1–s4 row objects match the baseline in both language versions where localized. Part 4 itself was already the unrounded endpoint calculation. Its new role is to supply a compulsory empirical judgment in part 5. The task text changes the introduction, adds material 4 and the pass notice, and replaces part 5. The solutions replace part 5 and add marking notes. The remaining deltas change the two descriptions from E.1/E.2 and 30 points to E.1 and 36, the coverage and strand lists, review metadata, scoring maxima, threshold and s5. The stable task ID and direct prerequisite IDs match the baseline.
partFourIntervalAndComparisonReview: Both factors are positive, so the corner products give the extrema of the stipulated input intervals. Using unrounded t₀ gives 7.8(t₀−0.03) = 3.7035865 m and 8.2(t₀+0.03) = 4.3855140 m. The outward centimetre interval is [3.70, 4.39] m. The exact width is 0.68193 m. The three measured intervals are [2.93, 3.03], [3.01, 3.11] and [2.88, 2.98] m. Even the highest endpoint is 0.59359 m below the exact prediction interval. The mean is 2.99 m, giving a nominal deficit of 1.04855 m or 26.0%. The quoted 0.13 m is the full maximum-to-minimum spread. The largest departure from the mean is 0.07 m. All three gate speeds lie within [7.8, 8.2] m/s. These results support incompatibility for the proposed use of the model under the stated uncertainty bounds. Three same-sided residuals establish a pattern in these trials. They do not distinguish a systematic measurement error from a model or reference-event error. Small rounding differences leave the comparison intact. The broader carry-forward rule can reverse it.
pointParticleAndRotationObservableReview:
The video reports the horizontal coordinate of S relative to the ramp edge at the instant any part of the car first touches the ground. It does not report the front's landing coordinate, the airborne displacement of S from release, or the duration of free flight. Parts 3–4 set x = 0 and t = 0 at an instantaneous horizontal point release and stop after a drop equal to the 1.25 m ramp height. For the car, the measured coordinate includes the horizontal offset of S at release. The time to first contact depends on the release height and velocity of S and the height of the lowest body point relative to S at contact. Uniform gravity gives the freely flying centre of mass a ballistic trajectory even while the car rotates. Fixed orientation can justify a matched drop of h with suitable level surfaces, initial contact geometry and launch conditions. Fixed orientation alone establishes neither that drop nor release of S at the edge. The 4.2 m length rules out a simple small-size argument relative to 4.04 m.

The wheelbase calculation gives 2.6/8.0 = 0.325 s, about 0.64t₀. It estimates the spacing in time between axle passages for nearly level motion at the stated speed. It does not measure rear-support duration, angular acceleration or downward release speed. With S midway between level axles, S would be approximately 1.3 m behind the edge at front-axle crossing and 1.3 m ahead at rear-axle crossing. A positive release offset can counteract a shorter airborne time. Front-first contact is consistent with forward pitch, but supplies neither its onset nor its angle. Release state, suspension and clearance, front contact geometry and orientation at touchdown can change the same observable. Under the additional point-origin and 8 m/s assumptions, 2.99 m would correspond to 0.374 s and a drop of 0.685 m. Those are conditional inferences, not video measurements. The timing ratio makes the transition worth considering. It cannot attribute several decimetres to one metre of shortening to that transition.
airResistanceBoundReview:
For the specified point launch and fixed drop, the horizontal displacement correction at fixed t₀ is bounded by ½(0.2)t₀² = 0.02548 m. K3 offers this as sufficient evidence about the total range, although vertical acceleration also changes the time available for horizontal travel. With ordinary still-air drag opposing rightward descent, horizontal drag shortens travel and upward drag delays contact. The maximum time is √(2.5/9.61) = 0.5100448 s. The delay of 0.0052260 s contributes at most +0.04181 m at 8 m/s. Evaluating the direct horizontal term even at that longer time gives at most 0.02602 m. Thus approximately −0.03 to +0.04 m is a reasonable scale under those sign assumptions. A strict upper bound rounded outward to centimetres is +0.05 m. The net sign is undetermined.

The team's component-magnitude bound alone also permits a sign-independent check. The shortest fixed-drop time is √(2.5/10.01) = 0.4997502 s. Bounding horizontal displacement at the time extrema gives corrections between −0.06553 and +0.06783 m at nominal speed. Even this conservative envelope is small relative to the 0.594 m gap and 1.049 m mean deficit. A few centimetres are comparable with the ±0.05 m measurement uncertainty, so the precision sought matters. The estimate bounds translational effects for matched launch and contact conditions. It supplies no bound on an aerodynamic pitching moment or on a change of first-contact geometry.
passBoundaryAndMissingCoreReview:
Let B be the sum of s1–s4. The old row maxima were 7, 6, 7, 6 and 4, with B ≤ 26. At 18/30, old s5 scores of 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 needed B ≥ 18, 17, 16, 15, 14 respectively. Parts 1–3 alone could pass with 20. At 28/36 the first four rows still total 26. Their share falls from 26/30 to 26/36, the pass fraction rises from 60% to 77.78%, and the allowable loss falls from 12 points to 8.

The authored s5 levels are 0 for no correct contribution, 1 for at least one but fewer than five core contributions, and 7 for all K1–K5. Only then do V1, V2 and V3 add one each, producing 8, 9 or 10. They concern the transition-time comparison, both drag effects, and a justified consequence respectively. For s5 = 0, 1, 7, 8, 9, 10 the necessary B is respectively 28, 27, 21, 20, 19, 18. The first two are impossible. With 7 all four old rows must contribute. With 8 either six-point row can be zero. With 9 or 10 any one old row can be zero. No two old rows can both be zero on a new pass. No individual V is compulsory. A correct isolated extension with no complete K is not expressly assigned a lower level, but the cap still applies. For any one K actually judged missing, the maximum is 26+1 = 27, including fractional scores within earlier row maxima. No fractional s5 level between 1 and 7 or rounding up to pass is authorized. The levels are in the row description. The numeric fields alone would also admit 26+2 = 28 if a grader disregarded that description.

The arithmetic protects the five marking decisions. K1 expressly asks for naming, and both names appear in the task, so recall can satisfy it. Copied assumptions alone fail K2 and K3. Yet K2 can credit an insufficient fixed-orientation argument, K3 can credit a horizontal-only bound, and K5 can credit unsupported causation while penalizing a scientifically justified finding of insufficient evidence. K4 has two conflicting instructions. For example, keeping parts 1–3 correct but transcribing ±0.03 s as ±0.30 s in part 4 gives [1.59, 6.60] m outward. All three observations fit that erroneous interval. The learner can conclude compatibility on their own figures, still discuss the 1.05 m shortfall from the correct nominal value and earn V1. With zero for s4, accepting K4 under the explicit carry-forward instruction allows 20+0+8 = 28. Enforcing K4's explicit actual-data conclusion caps s5 at 1 instead. Those two readings produce different pass decisions.
MODWholeGoalCoverageReview: The current MOD goal requires a learner to justify motion-model idealizations, including the point-particle approximation and neglect of friction, and identify where predictions reach their limits. Air resistance is a relevant friction example. Parts 5a–c genuinely ask for independent justification, a quantitative comparison and a limit tied to an observable. The data support a strong learner judgment that the ideal point launch misses the first-contact ranges and that bounded translational drag is too small to close the gap. Whole-MOD credit at pass is nevertheless indefensible for this exact file. The core permits incomplete reasoning about drag, rewards a causal attribution the data cannot resolve, and can accept a reversed empirical conclusion. Conversely, a learner who correctly explains the limits of identification risks losing the entire seven-point core. Retain this as evidence of intended MOD practice and withhold direct whole-goal credit.
fullPreparationAndSourceStageReview:
Traversing both direct requires lists reproduces exactly the 72 supplied prerequisite IDs, comprising 15 native Physics and 57 Mathematics goals. Horizontal projection leads to experimental free fall. MOD leads through the comparison of light and heavy falling bodies to the same free-fall goal. The closure includes motion laws, signed interval rates, mean and instantaneous speed, graph areas, measurement uncertainty and error types, with mathematics for functions, axes, areas, units and numerical operations. It supports the phase calculations, horizontal projection, endpoint comparison and elementary acceleration estimates. It does not teach a quantitative wheel-supported pitch and release model. More importantly, such a model would still need physical inputs absent here. A conditional explanation of why contact geometry matters needs no new course prerequisite.

Official HE Physics p. 30 places motion diagrams, uniform and accelerated motion, free fall, the neglect of rotation and extent in a point mass, and the neglect of friction in E.1. Horizontal projection, superposition and the x–y trajectory are E.3 on p. 31. The introductory mechanics programme spans E1/E2, with local sequencing subject to dependencies. An own voluntary HE E1 advanced offer is plausible after the explicit horizontal-projection preparation. The source does not designate this as an official E1 LK requirement. The learner analyses supplied gate readings and video-derived coordinates. There is no assessed learner-run experiment, determination of g, trajectory plot or required experimental design. Prerequisite status, PK1, strand tags and demand levels support planning and cannot establish those performances.
bilingualParityReview: DE and EN agree on the data, observable, calculations, threshold, K and V levels, and carry-forward permission. Both inherit the scientific and grading conflicts. The English statement that the car ‘leaves the edge horizontally’ especially suggests zero vertical velocity at actual release. The German ‘fährt … waagerecht über die Kante’ more readily describes the approach. Both keys then assert that S already moves downward at release. The event and the point whose velocity is specified need the same definition in both languages. The inherited structured descriptions s1–s4 are German only, with corresponding English worked solutions. The new s5 marking text is bilingual.
historicalResultRevisionReview: The baseline coveredGoalIds list is empty. Neither former claim, ce431132-dfc4-42c2-aff6-bd72035190f8 for experimental motion measurement and t–s representation nor e4b38061-1f28-43ad-8371-a3e7c0e81856 for the constant-acceleration model and its representations, reappears in the proposed list. Both remain in the prerequisite closure. The sole proposed addition is MOD. LI_MATERIE is removed from coveredStrands, leaving LI_BEWEGUNG and LI_TECHNIK. The stable assessment UUID spans materially different tasks, rubrics and cuts. Each stored attempt must retain its contemporaneous task, awarding rules, maximum, threshold, pass decision and credited goals. Neither an old pass nor an old raw score establishes performance on the new part 5. Any future MOD award needs evidence from the specific approved revision attempted.
requiredCorrections: Align material 4, part 5 and K2/K5 in both languages on the launch reference, the centre-of-mass state and the first-contact event. Credit the distinction between centre-of-mass translation and contact geometry.

Credit conditional mechanisms and justified non-identifiability. A compulsory sign, magnitude or causal attribution for the transition requires sufficient geometric and dynamical evidence. The present wheelbase estimate and first-contact observation do not supply it.

Require K3 to support its claim about range, including the possible time-of-flight effect. State the sign assumptions, accuracy scale and scope of the bound consistently in K3, V2 and the worked solutions.

Resolve K4 and carry-forward so a learner can receive method credit for consistent arithmetic while a pass carrying whole-MOD credit requires a valid judgment on the supplied data. Clarify that the pass notice refers to the five cores, with the three extensions optional.
Describe 0.13 m as the full observed spread and limit the systematic-deviation claim to the evidence from these trials. Keep causal remedies conditional.
Withhold the proposed MOD coverage on this exact revision. The content and rubric can be repaired while retaining the two direct prerequisites and the 28-point cut.
unsupportedOrUnderdeterminedInferences: The gate speeds and video endpoints do not establish the instant or position of final release, the release velocity vector of S, its fall distance or the airborne duration.

Front-first contact does not identify when pitch began, whether S was already descending at release, or how much pitch contributed to the signed range residual. A dimensionless time ratio is insufficient to establish a metre-scale correction.
A fixed orientation by itself does not establish simultaneous wheel contact after an S-drop of h. A change in orientation by itself does not invalidate ballistic centre-of-mass translation.

The supplied acceleration magnitude does not fix drag-component signs, aerodynamic torque or the total drag effect on a changing first-contact geometry. The data also do not validate the suggested changes to the car or ramp.
limits: The negative integrability decision applies to the exact file. The recommended 28 is the smallest integer cut above the incomplete-core maximum of 27. The cut does not resolve invalid core criteria.

This review uses the sealed baseline and context, the exact proposal, the supplied schema and the official HE source. Author release, status and review-note assertions carry no independent evidential weight.

The supplied record contains no deployed grader behavior, learner attempts, raw videos or independent verification of the team's drag estimate. Historical preservation is a requirement for using the revision, not an observed migration outcome.
The content finding concerns the intended own voluntary HE offer. Placement and applicability in other jurisdictions are outside its scope.
